title: LAUSD Ed learning acceleration chatbot and vendor continuity failure
system_purpose: Use district data and approved content to recommend personalized learning resources and support to students and families.
decision_impact: Recommendations could shape learning activities, family actions and requests for school support beyond normal school hours.
verified_facts: LAUSD announced Ed on 2024-03-20 for selected schools and stated that it analyzed grades, attendance and district offerings; later reporting states LAUSD disabled the chatbot after vendor AllHere laid off most employees.
reported_harm: Loss of service created continuity and governance risk; reporting also raised concern about stewardship of student data after the vendor's collapse, but this pack does not claim a confirmed privacy breach.
quantitative_evidence: The chatbot was publicly launched on 2024-03-20 and reported disabled on 2024-06-14, less than three months later.
limitations: LAUSD's launch claims are first-party and the shutdown evidence is secondary reporting; available sources do not quantify learning harm, prove a data breach or isolate a technical root cause.

title: Turnitin AI writing detector limitations in academic decisions
system_purpose: Estimate whether qualifying prose was likely generated or paraphrased by AI to support academic-integrity review.
decision_impact: A detector score can influence whether an educator opens a misconduct inquiry, requests explanation or takes an adverse academic action.
verified_facts: Turnitin release notes acknowledge false positives, hide numeric scores from 1 to 19 percent and state that an AI score should not be the sole basis for adverse action; a peer-reviewed study tested Turnitin with other detectors and rejected an easy reliable detection solution.
reported_harm: A false positive used without meaningful review can expose a student to an unfounded accusation, stress, dignity loss or opportunity loss; a false negative can undermine fair assessment.
quantitative_evidence: Turnitin suppresses displayed percentages in the 1 to 19 percent range; the peer-reviewed study considered 18 tools, excluded 6 and tested 12 available tools including commercial systems.
limitations: The study used a bounded mainly English-language corpus and tool versions have changed; the sources show reliability limitations but do not establish the false-positive rate for every institution or current model.
